title: Rubio in Mumbai as the US-India trade deal nears signing
deck: Washington says it is 'very close' to a trade deal with India, but the first tranche is still in legal drafting, and the US has tied its Russian-oil sanctions waivers to the talks while the Iran war keeps oil prices high.

fuel.title: Interim deal stuck on tariffs, politics
fuel.how: Sources and USTR Greer say unresolved tariff and political issues mean no immediate agreement, so the timing stays uncertain.

fuel.title: Rubio visits Jamnagar amid high oil
fuel.how: High oil prices from the Iran war push Washington to link energy interests, including Russian-oil waivers, to the trade deal.

card.headline: The US-India trade deal is close but not done, and oil is now part of the bargain

keyNumber.label: US tariff on Indian goods under the February 2026 framework, down from 25%; a separate 25% Russian-oil penalty was also removed

forYou.line: The 18% rate is the working number, but the first tranche is not signed. Plan for slippage, not a clean date.
Some Indian suppliers are already trying to cut US reliance; one Gap supplier wants to double its Europe share.
US waivers on Russian-energy sanctions are tied to the talks. A stall could raise sanctions risk on Indian crude buying.
Watch the Quad ministers' meeting and the 18-19 November Shenzhen summit. Both could move the deal's timing.
The Iran war keeps oil and freight costs high, which is why Washington and Delhi both want an energy understanding.

whatHappened: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on 19 October that Washington is 'very close' to finalising a trade deal with India. On 20 October he met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in Mumbai. A visit to the Jamnagar refinery was planned for 21 October.

The deal builds on a framework announced in February 2026. That framework cut the US reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from 25% to 18% and removed a separate 25% penalty tied to India's purchases of Russian oil. The first tranche of the actual agreement is still in legal drafting.

Signals since then are mixed. USTR Jamieson Greer said on 2 October that a deal was not imminent. On 26 October Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said most discussions are concluded and the agreement is being fine-tuned, and the White House called the talks productive. Greer also said the deal is nearing completion but no immediate agreement is expected. Reports say the interim deal remains stuck over tariffs and political concerns.
Rubio has explicitly tied US waivers on Russian-energy sanctions to the trade talks. Quad foreign ministers are due to meet in the US ahead of a leaders' summit.
whyItMatters: Trade: India is a large market and a manufacturing alternative to China. An 18% US tariff decides how Indian textiles, goods and services compete for US buyers against Chinese exporters, whose economy grew 4.5% in the third quarter on an export surge. Goyal's 'most talks concluded' makes a deal look near, but Greer's caution shows the last gaps are real.

Energy: US strikes on Iran began on 28 February 2026 and have kept oil and freight costs high for eight months. With Hormuz flows disrupted, India cannot easily replace Russian crude. That gives Washington a reason to ease sanctions on that oil and a way to use the waivers as leverage in the trade talks. Rubio's Jamnagar stop shows how closely energy and trade are linked.

Politics: The deal is a diplomatic prize on both sides. The Quad meeting adds momentum. But the reported stalemate over tariffs and political concerns, and criticism from a former Indian trade negotiator that Delhi must not sign a lopsided deal, show the limits. The deal also fits Trump's push to lock in bilateral tariff deals before the midterms and the Shenzhen APEC summit on 18-19 November.

winners.who: Indian exporters, if the 18% rate is locked in
winners.why: A clear, lower tariff than the 25% rate (and the extra 25% Russian-oil penalty) improves their position against Asian rivals.
A signed deal gives it a headline win before the midterms and leverage ahead of Shenzhen.

winners.who: Indian refiners with US-compatible sourcing, such as Jamnagar operators
winners.why: Waivers and a settled trade relationship could reduce sanctions risk, though details are unconfirmed.

losers.who: Chinese exporters competing for US import share
losers.why: An 18% rate for India narrows their relative tariff advantage in some categories. This is an inference, not a measured result.

losers.who: Indian firms that wait on the text
losers.why: Until the first tranche is signed, investment and pricing decisions stay on hold.
If India cuts its Russian crude purchases to meet US demands, they lose a large buyer. The waivers suggest the US may not demand this yet.

whatsNext: Late October to November: lawyers finish the first tranche; the key question is whether the signing date is announced.
3 November: US midterm elections. Trade announcements may be timed around them.
18-19 November: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen, with Trump due to attend. A China deal could change how Washington values an India deal.
Quad foreign ministers meet in the US ahead of the leaders' summit; the date of that summit is not confirmed in the material.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: when will the first tranche of the US-India deal most likely be signed?
options: Before the US midterms on 3 November
Between the midterms and the end of 2026
predict.explanation: Our base case is signing between the midterms and end-2026. Both sides say the text is nearly done, but Greer says nothing is imminent, and drafting and political disputes usually take weeks. The probability is our judgement, not a sourced forecast.

timeline.title: Analysts assess the US-India trade announcements
timeline.detail: The Stimson Center reviews the February framework, which cut the US reciprocal tariff on Indian goods from 25% to 18% and removed a separate 25% penalty tied to Russian oil.

timeline.title: Strikes on Iran begin
timeline.detail: The US-Israel war on Iran starts and, with disrupted Hormuz flows, keeps oil and freight costs elevated for the next eight months.

timeline.title: Greer says a deal is not imminent
timeline.detail: The US Trade Representative signals that the first tranche is still in legal drafting.

timeline.title: Rubio says the US is 'very close'
timeline.detail: The secretary of state speaks the day before his Mumbai visit.

timeline.title: Rubio meets Jaishankar in Mumbai
timeline.detail: The talks cover the trade deal and Russian-energy waivers, which Rubio explicitly ties to the trade negotiations.

timeline.title: Planned visit to the Jamnagar refinery
timeline.detail: Rubio was scheduled to visit the Jamnagar refinery. Wire headlines describe the trip as a turn to a small Indian city as the US faces high oil prices; we have not confirmed what was agreed there.

timeline.title: Quad ministers to meet; deal reported stuck
timeline.detail: Quad foreign ministers are set to meet in the US ahead of the leaders' summit. Separately, sources say the interim deal is stuck over tariffs and political concerns. Jaishankar says 'It's never done till it's done'.

timeline.detail: India's commerce minister says the agreement is now being fine-tuned. Greer says the deal is nearing completion but no immediate agreement is expected.

timeline.detail: Washington's response to Goyal's comments is positive but gives no signing date.

causes.name: US tariff strategy
causes.detail: The administration uses tariffs as leverage and wants bilateral deals with each partner.

causes.name: India's reliance on Russian crude
causes.detail: Cheap Russian oil became a large share of India's imports, and the US used a 25% penalty to pressure Delhi before removing it in February.

causes.name: Competition with China for US import share
causes.detail: Both countries sell similar categories of goods to US buyers, so tariff gaps matter.

causes.name: February framework
causes.detail: It set the 18% rate and dropped the Russian-oil penalty, but left details for later tranches.

causes.name: Drafting stage
causes.detail: The first tranche is in legal drafting, so a signing is near in principle but not scheduled.

causes.name: Iran war energy shock
causes.detail: Disrupted Hormuz flows and high oil prices make India's Russian crude harder to replace, so the US links waivers to the trade deal.

causes.name: US political calendar
causes.detail: Midterms on 3 November and the Shenzhen summit on 18-19 November create pressure to show trade wins.

causes.name: Diplomatic track
causes.detail: Rubio's visit and the Quad ministers' meeting add momentum to the relationship.

stakeholders.name: Marco Rubio
stakeholders.wants: A closed deal and Indian alignment on energy and security
stakeholders.leverage: Waivers on Russian-energy sanctions; the Quad track
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep pressing publicly that the deal is 'very close' while linking it to energy

stakeholders.name: Jamieson Greer
stakeholders.wants: A deal that meets US tariff and market-access aims
stakeholders.leverage: Control of the legal text and the tariff schedule
stakeholders.likelyMove: Stay cautious on timing, saying no immediate agreement is expected

stakeholders.name: S. Jaishankar
stakeholders.wants: A deal that preserves India's strategic autonomy
stakeholders.leverage: The Quad relationship and India's market size
stakeholders.likelyMove: Stress that nothing is final until signed

stakeholders.name: Piyush Goyal
stakeholders.wants: A signed first tranche that locks in the 18% rate
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep describing the talks as nearly complete

stakeholders.name: Indian refiners (e.g. Jamnagar operators)
stakeholders.role: Buyers of Russian and other crude
stakeholders.wants: Supply security and protection from sanctions risk
stakeholders.leverage: Large refining capacity that the US wants to see supplied
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep diversifying crude sources while waivers hold

stakeholders.name: Indian exporters
stakeholders.wants: A predictable US tariff and fewer extra duties
stakeholders.likelyMove: Diversify to Europe and other markets in case the deal slips

stakeholders.name: Moscow
stakeholders.wants: To keep India as a major buyer
stakeholders.likelyMove: Offer favourable terms to hold market share while the US wavers

sectors.why: A lower US tariff helps, but firms such as a Gap supplier are also looking to Europe to cut US reliance.
Waivers ease sanctions risk, but any US demand to cut Russian crude would raise costs while Hormuz flows are disrupted.

sectors.sector: US consumers and importers of Indian goods
sectors.why: A lower tariff than 25% (plus the Russian-oil penalty) lowers import costs, though the pass-through is unmeasured.
A lower tariff on Indian goods narrows China's relative advantage in categories where both compete for US import share.
A signed deal could raise India-US volumes, but war-driven freight costs remain high.
If India shifts away from Russian crude, supplies tighten; if waivers continue, little changes.

dailyLife.item: Prices of Indian-made clothing and goods in US shops
dailyLife.effect: A lower tariff can reduce costs for importers, but how much reaches shoppers depends on retailers and is not measured here.
The Iran war has kept oil and freight costs high for eight months; French diesel hit a record EUR 2.41 a litre in September, and Indian refiners face the same global market.
Textile and apparel workers depend on US orders, so a signed deal or a stall affects hiring. We have no figures.
High-level visits and the Quad meeting can speed visas and business links, but no concrete changes are announced.

scenarios.name: Signing before Shenzhen
scenarios.looksLike: The first tranche is signed in the weeks after the US midterms and before 18 November, with the 18% rate and energy language confirmed.
signposts: A signing date is announced by either side
Greer's language shifts from 'nearing completion' to 'finalised'
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Gives Trump a trade win before Shenzhen and reduces uncertainty for Indian exporters.

scenarios.name: Signing by early 2027
scenarios.looksLike: Drafting finishes after the midterms and the deal is signed between mid-November and end-January, perhaps alongside a Quad summit.
signposts: No new tariff threats against India
scenarios.effectOnWorld: A modest boost to India-US trade, with timing driven by diplomatic events.

scenarios.name: Drawn-out stalemate
scenarios.looksLike: Both sides keep saying 'nearly done' while disputes over tariffs and politics persist beyond the first quarter of 2027.
signposts: Domestic criticism of a lopsided deal grows
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Uncertainty persists and exporters diversify; waivers become the main bargaining chip.

scenarios.name: Breakdown
scenarios.looksLike: Talks collapse over Russian oil, tariffs or politics, and the US raises tariffs or ends the waivers.
signposts: Public disputes between Delhi and Washington
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Higher costs for Indian exporters, more Russian crude pressure and a setback for the Quad.

predictions.text: Probability 0.20: the first tranche of the US-India trade deal is signed before 18 November 2026.
Probability 0.55: the first tranche is signed by 31 January 2027.
Probability 0.75: the US keeps its 18% reciprocal tariff on Indian goods unchanged through the end of 2026.
Probability 0.60: US waivers on Russian-energy sanctions remain tied publicly to the India talks until the deal is signed.
Probability 0.50: the Quad leaders' summit takes place within six months, with the trade deal mentioned in the outcome.

actions: Price US contracts with the 18% rate as the base case and add a clause for tariff changes.
Build alternative markets, such as Europe, as some Indian suppliers are doing.
Watch energy and freight costs, which the Iran war keeps high.
Track Russian-oil sanctions language if your supply chain touches Indian refiners.
Treat 'nearing completion' statements as signals, not dates.
Watch Indian refiners and textile exporters for headline sensitivity.
Follow the Quad and Shenzhen calendars, which can shift timing.
Expect little direct effect on shop prices in the near term.
Plan for continued high fuel prices while the Iran war persists.
Publish the tariff schedule and energy terms clearly to reduce uncertainty.
Avoid signing a deal seen as lopsided; domestic critics warn against it.
Coordinate on energy supply so waivers do not create sudden cliffs.

analogues.whatFollowed: A headline framework was announced quickly, while fuller legal text and details took months to finalise.
Frameworks set tariff rates first, with details and implementation negotiated afterwards and sometimes disputed.

analogues.event: US sanctions waivers on Iranian oil for major buyers
analogues.whatFollowed: The US granted temporary waivers to large importers including India, then let them lapse, showing how waivers can serve as leverage.

watch.title: US midterm elections
watch.why: Trade announcements may be timed around the vote, and the result affects Trump's negotiating posture.

watch.title: APEC summit in Shenzhen begins
watch.why: A US-China exchange could change how Washington weighs the India deal; the summit runs 18-19 November.

watch.title: Quad foreign ministers' meeting in the US
watch.why: A date for the leaders' summit or trade language would signal momentum.

watch.title: US waivers on Russian-energy sanctions
watch.why: An extension, formalisation or lapse would show where energy and trade bargaining stands.

watch.title: Greer and Goyal statements
watch.why: A change from 'fine-tuning' and 'no immediate agreement' to a signing date would be the clearest signal.

watch.title: Oil and freight prices
watch.why: Further Gulf escalation raises India's need for Russian crude and the value of the waivers.

watch.title: Indian exporters' order books
watch.why: Shifts toward Europe or other markets would show how little exporters trust the timeline.

evidence.method: Drafted from the listed sources and the matched wire headlines, mostly secondary reports of statements by Rubio, Greer, Goyal and Jaishankar. No primary text of the agreement was available. Tariff rates come from the event summary and the Stimson analysis. Oil-market context comes from the connected event material. Scenario probabilities, prediction probabilities and sector directions are the author's estimates, and the Jamnagar visit outcome and the scope of the sanctions waivers could not be confirmed.
